newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - September 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - September 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not varified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Bangladesh parliament passed a bill for setting up a permanent commission to reform old and outdated laws or frame new ones suiting the present socio-economic conditions.
Asian Development Bank, a major financier to Bangladesh's energy sector, has asked the government to raise electricity tariff by 25 per cent and privatise power distribution in capital Dhaka.

Thousands of people in riverside areas remained marooned as floods in Northern districts deteriorated with continued swelling of the Ganges and Mahananda rivers. About 20,000 people in Rajshahi and Chapai Nawabganj districts are awaiting evacuation.

A ministerial-level meeting between Bangladesh and India is expected this month for reaching a permanent agreement on the sharing of Ganges water, Water Resources minister Abdur Razzak told the parliament.

Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has appealed to the opposition lawmakers to cooperate with her new government in the drive against "poverty, hunger and terrorism". As the first session of the current parliament was prorogued on Monday, Hasina, in her winding up speech, said she would run the government through "national consensus".
Indian Foreign Minister I K Gujral is due to arrive in Dhaka on September 6 on a four-day official visit to discuss bilateral issues with Bangladesh leaders.
Bangladesh parliament on Monday passed a bill allowing private companies to set up export processing zones.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina told visiting chairman of Peregrine Groups, Phillip Tose, that her government had taken business-friendly measures enabling local and foreign private investors o invest in the country.
